correctness.rationale: The unitary matrix formula is exact. Fourier block-phase pinching extracts diagonal and adjacent block subdiagonal trace norms as contractions on S1. The more distant lower blocks regroup exactly into rank-one row rectangles whose norms are bounded by adjacent blocks because the sum of polynomial column weights grows geometrically for a<1. Uniform block diagonal similarities compare all exponents, and a sparse h-indexed series proves loss of S2 at a=1 despite S1 at a=0. A 41,248-assertion finite checker confirms block identities, without replacing the infinite analytic proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2026 polynomial-weight invariance theorem is stated for 1<p<∞. General boundedness/compactness theorems do not imply S1 trace-norm summability, and small exponentially weighted Hardy-space hypotheses do not subsume arbitrary polynomial weights below exponent one. A general previously unknown abstract trace-ideal theorem remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 polynomial-weighted Rhaly theorem deliberately excludes the nuclear ideal endpoint p=1, where one cannot simply take a limit of Schatten estimates. The new dyadic trace-norm invariant handles all complex/nonmonotone coefficient sequences and proves membership is invariant across Hardy, weighted Bergman and positive-index Dirichlet Hilbert scales. The sharp failure at a=1 identifies the meaningful geometric threshold; the exact structural decomposition makes the criterion natural for research on factorable matrices rather than an isolated example.
